record.paper_title: Open Problems on Syzygies and Hilbert Functions
record.original_question: Construct families of homogeneous ideals whose regularity grows polynomially, exponentially, or doubly exponentially in the number of variables while the largest degree among the minimal homogeneous generators remains bounded by a fixed constant.

artifact.status_search_result: Doubly exponential growth of regularity with bounded generator degree is known via Mayr–Meyer type constructions (e.g., Bayer–Stillman, Koh), matching the Galligo–Giusti–Caviglia–Sbarra upper bound $(2d)^{2^{n-2}}$. Singly exponential and polynomial-growth families with bounded generator degrees can also be exhibited, but a unified, explicit construction yielding each prescribed growth rate (polynomial, exponential, doubly exponential) with a fixed degree bound is regarded as a problem to construct rather than a single solved theorem.

status_evidence.title: The Regularity Conjecture for Prime Ideals in Polynomial Rings
status_evidence.snippet: reg(I) ≤ (2d)^{2^{n-2}} (Galligo–Giusti, Caviglia–Sbarra). The Mayr–Meyer example shows the doubly exponential behavior cannot be avoided.
status_evidence.claim: Doubly exponential growth of regularity with bounded generator degree is achieved by Mayr–Meyer-style examples.

status_evidence.title: Bounds for the Castelnuovo-Mumford regularity of modules
status_evidence.snippet: In general, the regularity of a module can be doubly exponential in the degrees of the minimal generators and in the number of variables.
status_evidence.claim: Doubly exponential lower bounds in n with fixed generator degree are known.
